purpose: Minimal high-value runtime probes for behavior that static/source proof cannot fully emulate. These are not NEED_VALIDATION findings and do not change canonical report counts unless runtime evidence reveals a contradiction.

policy.promoteOnlyAfter: runtime observation → source cross-check → Claim-Based Proof → canonical BUG/DESIGN_MISMATCH/DEV NOTE

priorityA.exactQuestion: Does disconnecting during the cutscene/session-admission transition leave the resumed gameplay state fully initialized?
priorityA.startState: Reach a normal cutscene immediately before active gameplay or the next authored gameplay phase.
steps: Disconnect while the cutscene is still active.
Stay offline until the cutscene would normally finish.
Reconnect to the same session.
Continue the first gameplay action after the transition.
priorityA.observableA: The cutscene/transition resumes or reconciles cleanly and the next gameplay phase behaves normally.
priorityA.observableB: The phase advanced while offline and one or more gameplay systems are missing, stale, blocked, duplicated, or desynchronized.
priorityA.whyHighValue: Circuit exposed a real offline-transition defect. FOP2 has an explicit cutscene/session-admission lifecycle and reconnect handling, so this is a direct high-value cross-map probe.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: Native timing plus the final in-game reconstruction/interaction outcome is best checked in runtime even though source closure found no contradiction.

priorityA.exactQuestion: Can a player disconnect/reconnect around bed destruction or elimination and end in a state that disagrees with the authoritative team/respawn state?
priorityA.startState: Two teams active; target player still has a live bed and is participating normally.
steps: Destroy the target player's/team bed near the same time the target player dies or disconnects.
Reconnect the target player immediately after the bed state changes.
Observe respawn/elimination behavior.
Check whether team/objective/UI state agrees with whether respawn is still allowed.
priorityA.observableA: Bed state, player elimination, respawn permission, and UI all agree.
priorityA.observableB: Player respawns when no longer eligible, is eliminated while still eligible, or objective/UI state disagrees with the actual lifecycle.
priorityA.whyHighValue: This combines objective terminal state, death/respawn and reconnect—three material Bedwars systems already identified by the audit.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: The selected artifact had no source-proven race, but real event ordering and native death/disconnect timing can expose a mismatch.

priorityA.exactQuestion: Can kit/equipment state be retained, duplicated, or lost across death plus reconnect?
priorityA.startState: Select a non-default kit/loadout and enter active combat.
steps: Change or equip a managed kit/loadout.
Die or enter the map's normal death/respawn lifecycle.
Disconnect before or during the restore/respawn boundary.
Reconnect and inspect inventory, armor/equipment, and active kit state.
priorityA.observableA: Exactly one valid kit is present and all kit/equipment state matches the authoritative selection.
priorityA.observableB: Old and new kit items coexist, required equipment is missing, or UI/selection state disagrees with inventory/equipment.
priorityA.whyHighValue: The map has explicit kit/loadout, combat, reconnect and fresh-session state surfaces but no runtime ground truth yet.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: Static proof closed without a contradiction; the probe targets native inventory timing and actual reconnect sequencing.

priorityA.map: Five Nights at Z Village Level 2
priorityA.exactQuestion: Do remote spawned enemies continue simulating and allow the defense wave to progress when the player remains at the normal defense/base position?
priorityA.startState: Start the first representative defense wave from the authored player position.
steps: Do not move toward the remote enemy spawn area.
Let the wave run from the intended defense/base location.
Observe whether enemies path/attack and whether wave accounting advances.
Repeat once after a retry or second run if the first pass succeeds.
priorityA.observableA: Enemies remain active, reach/engage the objective, and wave completion accounting progresses normally.
priorityA.observableB: Enemies freeze/despawn/stall outside simulation range or wave progression blocks while the player stays in the intended play area.
priorityA.whyHighValue: The map materially depends on residency, remote simulation and wave accounting. Native simulation behavior is one of the highest-value runtime-only surfaces.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: Source coverage found no contradiction, but actual Bedrock simulation distance/residency behavior is engine-native.

priorityA.exactQuestion: Does an equipment/economy upgrade remain atomic if the player disconnects immediately after purchase?
priorityA.startState: Player has enough currency for one weapon or armor upgrade.
steps: Purchase one upgrade.
Disconnect immediately after the purchase is accepted.
Reconnect to the same active session.
Compare currency, equipment tier, inventory item, and any upgrade/UI state.
priorityA.observableA: Currency and upgraded equipment commit exactly once and all representations agree.
priorityA.observableB: Currency is deducted without the item, upgrade duplicates, old equipment remains alongside new equipment, or UI/tier state disagrees.
priorityA.whyHighValue: Orb L2 already demonstrated a real transactional upgrade defect. Orb L1 has equivalent economy/equipment surfaces but no source-proven issue.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: This is a metamorphic cross-level probe aimed at native interruption timing, not an asserted L1 bug.

priorityA.exactQuestion: Does a key/item-driven puzzle remain consistent across an active-session world reload?
priorityA.startState: Acquire or activate a material key/item/mechanism but stop before the next puzzle/terminal commit.
steps: Reach a state where the key/item or mechanism is acquired/activated.
Reload/re-enter the world while the session is still logically in progress.
Continue the same puzzle interaction.
Check inventory/item state, mechanism/world state, and progression.
priorityA.observableA: The item/mechanism and progression state reconstruct to one coherent state and the puzzle remains completable.
priorityA.observableB: Item exists but mechanism resets, mechanism remains active but item/progression resets, or the puzzle becomes duplicated/stuck.
priorityA.whyHighValue: Clockwork Vault explicitly combines key/item lifecycle, entity/mechanism state, world mutation and active-session reload.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: Static closure found no contradiction; actual world/entity restoration order is valuable to verify once in runtime.

priorityA.exactQuestion: Can reconnect during a round transition leak the prior round's loadout/score/state into the next round?
priorityA.startState: Reach the end of one round with non-default loadout or non-zero score/progress.
steps: Trigger normal round completion.
Disconnect during the transition before the next round is fully ready.
Reconnect after the next round has started or is preparing.
Check loadout, score/reward state, team/participant state, and next-round readiness.
priorityA.observableA: Only intended cross-round state survives; next-round loadout and progression are correct.
priorityA.observableB: Old loadout/resources remain, required new state is missing, reward/score commits twice, or the player is not correctly assigned to the new round.
priorityA.whyHighValue: The map has explicit round transitions, loadout, score/reward, reconnect and repeated-run state but no runtime ground truth.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: The test stresses a real transition boundary whose final timing/interaction is runtime-specific.

priorityA.exactQuestion: Does a second run begin from the same effective world/objective baseline as the first run?
priorityA.startState: Complete one normal run far enough to mutate world/objective/entity state.
steps: Finish or reset the first run normally.
Start a second run without re-importing/restarting the world.
Compare the initial objective/world state with the first run.
Attempt the first progression interaction of the second run.
priorityA.observableA: Second-run world, entities, objectives and player state match the authored fresh baseline.
priorityA.observableB: A world mutation/entity/objective from run 1 survives or a required run-2 state is missing/duplicated.
priorityA.whyHighValue: Aftershock contains explicit world mutation/reset, entity lifecycle, reconnect and reload surfaces and currently has only a prospective zero-finding snapshot.
priorityA.runtimeOnlyReason: Second-run world persistence is a high-yield native-runtime probe after static reset proof closes.

priorityB.exactQuestion: Does reload during a stage transition preserve exactly one valid objective/progression state?
priorityB.reason: Stage progression + spatial/world mutation + reload recovery are all material surfaces.

priorityB.exactQuestion: After developer fix, can one cooperative player still damage another?
priorityB.reason: Regression verification only; current canonical artifact already has a PROVEN friendly-fire bug.

executionRule: Run Priority A in order. Stop expanding manual coverage when repeated probes are clean unless new runtime evidence creates a new generalized regression family.

resultHandling.clean: Record PASS only; do not create a DEV NOTE merely because runtime was tested.
resultHandling.contradiction: Record exact observation, then source-crosscheck before publishing.
resultHandling.ambiguous: Capture exact state and observable; do not use generic NEED_VALIDATION.
